findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit Approach step retargeting `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py:126-134` from `rebar untag <id> <tag>` to `rebar edit <id> --remove-tag <tag>` (and update its help text at :45,74).
evidence: Scope lists `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py` but Approach steps (1)-(6) never mention it
findings.finding: `scripts/retarget_jira_project.py:130` shells out `subprocess.call(["rebar", "untag", ticket_id, tag])` (with usage/help strings at :45,74,126,134 naming `rebar untag`). The plan lists this file in Scope but neither the Approach nor Testing describes retargeting its `untag` invocation to `edit --remove-tag`; after the hard cutover this script would exit 2 on every tag strip.
scenarios: Operator runs `retarget_jira_project.py --strip-tags` after cutover; every `rebar untag` subprocess exits 2
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the subprocess argv with `["rebar", "edit", ticket_id, "--remove-tag", tag]`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the new `check_cli(argv, tracker, repo_root)` forwards (argv, tracker) to the 2-arg `check_ac_cli`/`quality_check_cli` and (argv, tracker, repo_root) to the 3-arg `clarity_check_cli`, and add an end-to-end `main(["check", <id>, ...])` dispatch assertion mirroring the resolve TypeError check.
evidence: gates.py:82 `def check_ac_cli(argv: list[str], tracker: str) -> int`
gates.py:211 `def clarity_check_cli(argv: list[str], tracker: str, repo_root: str | None) -> int`
gates.py:388 `def quality_check_cli(argv: list[str], tracker: str) -> int`
_execute.py:122 `return fn(rest, tracker, None)` for adapter argv_tracker_root
Plan: 'delegating to the unchanged check_ac_cli, clarity_check_cli, quality_check_cli'
findings.finding: The `check` route is declared with adapter="argv_tracker_root" (3-arg call fn(rest, tracker, None)) and delegates to three handlers whose live signatures differ in arity: check_ac_cli(argv, tracker) and quality_check_cli(argv, tracker) are 2-arg, while clarity_check_cli(argv, tracker, repo_root) is 3-arg. The plan calls these three 'unchanged' and introduces a new check_cli, but does not spell out that check_cli must bridge the arity mismatch (forwarding only (argv, tracker) to the two 2-arg handlers). A reader could wire the 3-arg adapter to a 2-arg handler and hit a TypeError.
findings.location: Approach step (3): check-ac/clarity-check/quality-check become one `check` route; Scope src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py
scenarios: check_cli dispatches to check_ac_cli with the 3-arg adapter's full tuple

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the default output of plain `rebar resolve <id>` (no --display) after the fold — canonical id vs config-driven _display_mode — and add a byte-equality assertion pinning that default.
evidence: AC asserts only exit 0 for `main(["resolve", <id>])`, not output bytes
findings.finding: Folding `format` into `resolve --display[=MODE]` changes the default output of plain `rebar resolve <id>`: the current resolve_cli prints the resolved canonical id, whereas format_cli's no-mode default is `_display_mode(repo_root)` (config-driven: auto/canonical/alias/short). The plan hosts the folded `_display_mode(repo_root)` call in resolve_cli but does not state whether plain `resolve <id>` (no --display) preserves the old canonical-id output or adopts format's config-driven default — a user-visible semantic change.
findings.location: Approach step (3): format folded into `resolve --display[=MODE]`; AC: main(["resolve", <id>]) exits 0
scenarios: A caller relying on `rebar resolve <id>` emitting the canonical id gets a config-driven alias/short form instead
